draft.title: Communicating across cultures
card: Cultures differ in words, gestures, tone and ideas about what is polite. A message can be understood in a way the speaker did not mean.
paying close attention to what the other person says and how they say it, before replying or judging.
checking what someone means instead of guessing. Polite, open questions show respect and clear up confusion.

finding out about other cultures, such as customs and values, before and during contact. In a globalised world, where people from many cultures meet more often, this can help people communicate respectfully.
draft.remember: Listen, ask and learn, so you check meaning instead of assuming it.

a.q: Kofi starts work with a team from several cultures. He is unsure what a colleague meant by a gesture. What is the best way to communicate respectfully?
opts: Politely ask the colleague what they meant
Decide what it meant based on his own culture
Copy the gesture back without asking about it
Avoid talking to the colleague from then on
a.why: Asking a polite question checks the meaning instead of guessing. Using his own culture to decide what it meant risks the very misunderstanding the card describes.
a.clue: Which choice checks the meaning instead of guessing it?

b.q: Mei is about to host exchange students from Peru. Before they arrive she reads about greetings and meal customs in Peru. Which habit is she mainly using?
opts: Learning about another culture in advance
Listening closely to what a person says
Avoiding contact until she feels ready
b.why: Mei is finding out about customs before contact, which is learning about another culture. Asking and listening happen in a conversation with a person, and she has not yet met the students.
b.clue: Which habit happens before any conversation takes place?

a.best: Politely ask the colleague what they meant

b.best: Learning about another culture in advance
